text: However, an employment-related practices exclusion (see ¶ 3:318 ff.) may bar coverage even for post-termination tort claims. (See further discussion at ¶ 3:390 ff.) c. [3:425] “Intentional injury” exclusion: Tort claims incidental to termination of employment may also be excluded from CGL “bodily injury” coverage by the express exclusion for “intentional injury” (see ¶ 3:311) or the implied exclusion for “wilful acts” created by Ins.C. § 533 (see ¶ 3:105 ff.). • [3:426] A termination of employment in violation of public policy (so-called Tameny tort) is deemed inherently harmful as a matter of law and insurance coverage is therefore barred by Ins.C. § 533: “Under any reasonable criterion, a termination in violation of such public policies must be held wrongful as a matter of law.” [B & E Convalescent Ctr. v. State Comp. Ins. Fund (1992) 8 CA4th 78, 99, 9 CR2d 894, 907—involving workers' compensation and employers' liability policy rather than CGL policy, but court noted that differences in policies did not affect application of Ins.C. § 533] [3:427 - 3:439] Reserved. 4.
